column1: # THE REPAIR STRIDE -- PO-78's repair phase.  Set at r7329, re-cut to two seats at r7331,
#   RE-CUT TO THREE SEATS AT r7339 when the secondment's return trigger fired.  Data, not code.
# ** THIS IS THE WHOLE LIST AND IT IS NOT A TRIAGE. **  Every REPAIR-OWED row in
#   corpus/quote_pin_baseline.tsv is on it.  AT r7339: 284 rows in 90 receipts over 53 prefixes,
#   down from 366 in 135 at r7329 -- 82 rows and 45 receipts cleared in two revisions, and NOTHING
#   cleared at r7339, because both repair seats spent the revision on pre-registrations.  A row
#   leaves by being REPAIRED or by being WITHDRAWN with its case written down beside the repair --
#   never by reclassification and never by looking hard at it.
# ** THE UNIT IS THE RECEIPT, NOT THE ROW, AND THE BALANCE IS ON RECEIPTS. **  A repair edits a receipt's
#   assertions, so a receipt holding five owed rows is one repair touching five keys.  Median 2 rows a
#   receipt, mean 3.16 at r7339, max 12; 12 of the 90 receipts hold exactly one.  The whole list splits
#   171 PAPER / 113 SOURCE and 188 SENTENCE / 96 TOKEN.  r7329's first cut
#   balanced on ROWS and came out 74 receipts against 61 -- balancing on the wrong unit, caught in the
#   same cycle.  The three-seat cut below is 30 receipts a seat exactly, and the rows fall where the
#   receipts put them: 90, 89 and 105, which is 3.00, 2.97 and 3.50 rows a receipt.
# ** THREE SEATS FROM r7339.  THE SECONDMENT IS DISCHARGED. **  70 was seconded to the Lean line's
#   campaign 2 at r7331 with the return trigger "when the last three reopenable rows land".  They
#   landed: 70 took row 72, 71 took 59 and 62, and 71's census reads REOPENABLE 0 at r7337+71.3.  So
#   70 returns to the repair stride here and the cut goes to three seats in the same revision, as
#   r7337's clause said it would.  70 keeps the nightly at 11:00 UTC.  Node 71 is not on this stride
#   -- it has the Lean census and campaign 3.  Node 69 is not a workhorse and takes none.
# ** THE RE-CUT RULE, FROM r7333, AND IT BINDS THIS RE-CUT. **  A stride re-cut applies to work NOT YET
#   BEGUN, and the blocks a seat was told to do FIRST under the old cut stay that seat's.  Held here:
#   cc66 keeps P15_CR_cosmology, whose last 12 receipts it pre-registered at r7337+cc66; 60 keeps
#   L165/L211/L175/L204, the 19 receipts it pre-registered at r7338.  Those 31 receipts were not
#   available to the re-cut and 70's 30 come entirely from the unbegun 59.  r7331 reassigned
#   L147_two_arm to 60 and told it to start there while 70 was already working it under r7329's order;
#   both seats repaired the same 13 rows.  A re-cut that reassigns the head of a seat's queue is a
#   re-cut that will be raced.
# ** AFFINITY, AND IT IS WEAKER THAN IT WAS. **  cc66 holds P15_CR_cosmology and its own sector
#   prefixes; 60 holds the L165/L175/L211/L204 block it verdicted.  70's 30 are the unbegun tail and
#   carry no affinity claim beyond L202/L_probability, which it has read this revision.  A repair wants
#   the seat that verdicted the prefix, because the repairer has to recognise what the check was trying
#   to assert -- but 59 of 90 receipts had no begun claim on them, so most of this cut is balance.
# ** WHAT A REPAIR IS. **  THE_RULE.md at 1a3c13a61 is the WORKING RULE, adopted at r7329 and refined in
#   use.  A repair makes the check assert what the claim IS rather than that a sentence is present --
#   the form 60 used on its own S45 key at r7330.  Where the rule owes a repair that should not be owed,
#   or misses one it should catch, the case is written down beside the repair and the rule is amended
#   from those cases in small named changes.  The text stays applied throughout.
# ** AND NO INTER-RATER MEASURE GOVERNS A REPAIR (r7333). **  Both those L147 repairs pass all five
#   receipts while agreeing on 48-78 per cent of what to remove and on 2 replacement literals of
#   fifty-odd: a repair has many correct outputs where a verdict had one.  The arbiter is the 134-gate
#   sweep plus the carry ledger (git fetch origin refs/ci/carry && git show FETCH_HEAD:carry.json),
#   per repair.
# ** AND TWO QUANTITIES, NEITHER STANDING FOR THE OTHER (r7333, r7337). **  Report EFFORT and REALISED
#   receipts a revision with the assignment named; and report the owed count BESIDE the keys minted and
#   adjudicated, because a repair clears a row either by making the check assert the claim in a form the
#   instrument reads or by restructuring it out of pin form -- both repairs, only the first visible.
# ** WHAT A REPAIR WRITES, AS AMENDED TWICE. **  THE_RULE.md (r7335, 69 from 60's case): the SHORTEST
#   span that carries the whole claim and occurs once under the checker's own normalisation, and then
#   STOP.  r7339 rules on cc66's routed case against it and the second amendment is owed from 69:
#   A LOCUS-SCOPED CONJUNCTION OF SPANS SATISFIES THE FLOOR.  cc66's locus-scoped form asserts a unique
#   prose locator and the claim's value within ONE locus; all 13 of its locators are unique and only 4
#   of its 12 value fragments are, so read as requiring ONE CONTIGUOUS span the floor owes 8 of 25
#   again -- all 8 failures being the asserted ATOM and none the statement that says it.  Measured at
#   r7339: uniqueness alone costs 0.6x the pair form's characters -- the growth is CONTIGUITY, not
#   uniqueness, and contiguity was never a stated requirement.  The minimand is TOTAL
#   PINNED CHARACTERS, not the number of spans.  Until 69's text lands, a locus-scoped repair is
#   compliant and is not re-opened -- EXCEPT C40, which has no unique anchor at all (its one span,
#   "against the measured", stands 8 times), so there is nothing for the within-locus condition to
#   attach to and that row is genuinely still owed.  7 retired, 1 standing.
# ** AND EVERY COUNT UNDER THE FLOOR IS REPORTED NORMALISED (r7339, cc66's). **  check_quote_pins's
#   _unmark is many-to-one, so a span's normalised count can only RISE: a raw count is a LOWER bound on
#   the count the floor is tested against.  Verified on cc66's 25 spans -- one case, the theta ratio,
#   twice raw and three times normalised.
